entries.gave: The vision serves the accountant, who prints each client invoice at that client tax rate without help, and the installer, who sets up the command on each accountant machine; invoicer maintainers read it to lean each choice. Read docs/product-vision.md whole and both Mores kept (product-vision N6 on decision 5/3, refactor-doc N8 on decision 0/3); no inputs.
Read product-vision best-practice.md with its template.md, and refactor-doc best-practice.md, to their end.
The job, from N1 decision 0: invoicer gives the accountant a command that prints a client invoice from the invoice lines they keep in a spreadsheet, at that client tax rate.
Roles named by their job, from N1 decision 2: accountant, one who prints a client invoice; installer, one who sets up the command on each accountant machine.
The accountant prints only once the installer has set up the command, per N1 decision 1, so the installer stays a role.
No person job is left unclear; the decisions settle both roles, so nothing to ask.
No split: every accountant counts a printed correct invoice as the job done.
No merge: the installer counts a ready machine, the accountant a printed invoice.
Two roles, so neither is named user.
O1 and O2 taken from N2 decisions 0 and 1, each with its role as subject.
Each objective ends in the role own work: a client gets a correct invoice; a machine is ready to print.
Two distinct ends, as a setup can finish with no invoice printed; one objective each.
Tasks from N4 decision 0: invoice lines and the client tax rate to the printed invoice; a bare machine to the accountant running the command.
KR1.1 and KR2.1 measure the failing share, per N4 decision 1.
KR1.2 and KR2.2 measure the time with the role own time included, per N4 decision 1.
Each key result says Lower is better.
KR1 ranks before KR2 within each objective, stated once in the template ranking line, kept as the person chose.
No targets; the template line gives the plain reason.
Pieces from N5 decision 0: the invoice command, the README part for the accountant, the README setup section.
The command and the README accountant part serve O1; the setup section serves O2.
The setup section serves O2 without O1, so the two stay apart.
Each idea marked for O1 alone, per N6 decision 3, as the accountant meets each at every print and the installer once.
Every piece serves an objective; nothing to ask.
The one way and the ideas come from the person, held in N6 decisions 0 and 1; no new question.
The one way kept in one sentence: invoicer command prints the finished invoice from the invoice lines and the client tax rate.

Each of the three ideas gets what it gives the accountant toward a correct invoice, and what it spares the installer where it spares something, per N6 decision 3 and the N6 More; the rate idea now says why: the client tax rate differs from client to client.
Moments from N6 decision 2: the installer sets up and sees it run; the accountant gives the invoice lines and the client tax rate; the invoice prints, or a message says what to fix.
Setup is held by the spreadsheet-as-is and the rate-each-time ideas (nothing to set up); giving input by the spreadsheet-as-is idea; the print by nothing-wrong-prints. Every moment has an idea.
No idea proposed; all three are the person own, so nothing to ask.
All three ideas kept; the one way would fail at a moment without any one of them.
docs/product-vision.md read to its end: Roles names who it serves, Objectives and key results what they reach and how it is measured, Concept the one way and its ideas.
Readers, from the Cut name: the accounting team, who check that it serves their printing, and invoicer maintainers, who lean each choice on it.
Accountants know invoices, spreadsheets and tax rates, not Python; maintainers know the code and come to learn whom it serves and why each idea holds.
The template three sections each hold one topic; no split.
Each idea has its own list item with its name, so a reader finds it; headings stay the template ones.
Roles, objectives and ideas are items in no order, so bulleted lists; no steps or comparisons call for another form.
Readers words come from the person request: invoice, invoice lines, spreadsheet, tax rate, client.
Words chosen from the person request: the client tax rate, the invoice line, the spreadsheet; no value, no unreadable rate.
The fact that the accountant installs nothing sits in the installer role alone; the idea lines say only what each idea spares the installer.
Each fact keeps one place: the roles in Roles, the measures in key results, the why of each idea in its line.
No two places state a fact differently; nothing to ask.
Grouped names: line, value and rate in the Nothing wrong prints idea; rate alone in the rate idea; spreadsheet and sheet.
Kept, per N1 decision 3: the client tax rate, the invoice line, the spreadsheet; value, rate alone and line alone dropped.
No name refers to two things once value is gone.

Each Cut decision taken as it stands. Settled without asking: each idea line gets two short sentences, the accountant gain then the installer one; idea names follow the names rule. No point left open.
